input_text: Corporation A decides to sue Corporation B for stealing trade secrets. To prove that B did it, lawyers for A introduce as evidence a statement made by B's CEO to one of his friends that B "would soon have the ability to compete with A."

extraction.input_text: Corporation A decides to sue Corporation B for stealing trade secrets. To prove that B did it, lawyers for A introduce as evidence a statement made by B's CEO to one of his friends that B "would soon have the ability to compete with A."

claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The statement was made out of court by B's CEO to a friend.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a) and 801(c) require an out-of-court statement for hearsay analysis.
arguments.evidence_span: statement made by B's CEO to one of his friends

arguments.text: The statement contains an assertion that B "would soon have the ability to compete with A."
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires the statement to be one that the declarant asserts.
arguments.evidence_span: statement made by B's CEO to one of his friends that B "would soon have the ability to compete with A."

arguments.text: The statement is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted, specifically to establish B's capability to steal trade secrets.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires the statement to be offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.evidence_span: To prove that B did it, lawyers for A introduce as evidence a statement

arguments.text: The statement qualifies as a party-opponent admission under FRE 801(d)(2) because it was made by B's CEO, an agent of Corporation B.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(d)(2) excludes statements made by a party's agent or employee concerning a matter within the scope of that relationship from the definition of hearsay.
